Part I — Public partner page1. Partner Program

Prove Your Potential. Build What’s Next.

At UzLeeder, we believe meaningful partnerships are built through ability, accountability, trust, and shared ambition.

We welcome people who can turn ideas into working solutions, solve real problems, and contribute to the development of technology and digital products.

Our Partner Program is designed for developers, AI engineers, designers, product builders, researchers, technical specialists, and other qualified individuals or organizations who want to collaborate with UzLeeder.

We don't select partners on promises alone. We evaluate what they can demonstrate.

Applicants enter a structured qualification process to demonstrate their skills, working standards, communication, and potential contribution to the UzLeeder ecosystem.

Submitting an application does not guarantee acceptance.

Who can apply?

We welcome applications from individuals, independent professionals, teams, and eligible organizations with relevant skills, experience, or a credible plan to develop them.

Potential areas of collaboration include:

  • Web and mobile application development.
  • SaaS products and digital platforms.
  • AI-powered applications and automation.
  • Software architecture and engineering.
  • UI/UX design and product development.
  • Cybersecurity and responsible technology practices.
  • Research, business analysis, and product strategy.
  • Marketing, growth, and other relevant business functions.

Applicants are evaluated according to the role, project, and collaboration opportunity. Applicants do not need to demonstrate every skill listed above.

2. How the Program Works

Step 1 — Apply

Submit your application with relevant information about your background, skills, experience, portfolio, interests, and intended contribution.

Step 2 — Review the Policy

Read the Partner Program Policy, applicable confidentiality and security requirements, privacy notice, and qualification terms.

Acknowledge the applicable conditions before entering the qualification stage.

Step 3 — Choose or Receive a Qualification Project

Depending on the role and the needs of UzLeeder, you may follow one of two pathways.

Path A: UzLeeder-Assigned Project

UzLeeder provides a defined project brief based on a genuine organizational or product need. The brief specifies the expected deliverables, acceptance criteria, timeline, available resources, and applicable compensation and intellectual-property terms.

Path B: Independent Project Proposal

You propose an idea and develop a project that demonstrates your abilities. You explain the problem, intended users, solution, implementation, technical decisions, and potential value of the work.

Your project may be an application, platform, prototype, or another relevant deliverable.

UzLeeder may approve your proposed idea, request modifications, or recommend an assigned project instead.

Step 4 — Demonstrate Your Abilities

Depending on the role, your work may be evaluated for:

  • Functionality and quality of the deliverable.
  • Technical competence and problem-solving.
  • Architecture, maintainability, and documentation.
  • Security, privacy, and responsible development.
  • Creativity and product thinking.
  • Communication and collaboration.
  • Reliability, ownership, and response to feedback.

The assessment criteria will be communicated before the relevant challenge begins.

Step 5 — Receive a Decision

After reviewing the evidence, UzLeeder may approve the applicant, request further information, offer another qualification opportunity, decline the application, or keep it pending where appropriate.

Successful qualification does not by itself establish a legal partnership, employment relationship, equity interest, or guaranteed commercial opportunity.

Step 6 — Formalize the Partnership

Applicants selected for partnership receive the applicable written agreement and onboarding instructions.

The agreement defines the actual relationship, responsibilities, permissions, compensation or equity arrangements where applicable, intellectual-property terms, confidentiality obligations, and termination conditions.

A partnership becomes effective only according to the applicable agreement and its acceptance requirements.

3. What We Expect from Partners

We value people who:

  • Represent their skills and experience honestly.
  • Deliver work according to agreed requirements.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally.
  • Respect confidential information and intellectual property.
  • Follow agreed security and privacy practices.
  • Accept constructive feedback.
  • Take responsibility for their decisions and commitments.
  • Respect other contributors and collaborate in good faith.
  • Identify limitations, risks, and problems rather than concealing them.

We evaluate actual contributions and relevant evidence rather than promises, prestige, or unsupported claims.

4. What Applicants Can Expect from UzLeeder

UzLeeder aims to provide:

  • A clearly described qualification process.
  • Relevant requirements and evaluation criteria before work begins.
  • Reasonable communication about progress and decisions.
  • Appropriate access to resources required for an authorized project.
  • Clear written terms concerning compensation, ownership, and use of submitted work.
  • Respectful treatment and protection of application information.
  • Feedback where reasonably available.
  • A defined process for moving from qualification to a formal partnership.

Specific opportunities, resources, compensation, mentorship, and future projects depend on the written terms and actual availability. They are not guaranteed merely by applying.

5. Apply to Become a Partner

If you are ready to demonstrate your abilities and contribute to meaningful technology projects, submit an application through the UzLeeder Partner Program.

Your application will be reviewed according to the relevant requirements and opportunities.

Part II — Official Partner Program Policy6. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes the principles, eligibility requirements, qualification procedures, assessment standards, and general conduct expected within the UzLeeder Partner Program.

It applies to applicants and participants in the program, including individuals, teams, and organizations where relevant.

Additional terms may apply to specific projects, contracts, data access, software repositories, client engagements, or commercial relationships.

Where a signed project agreement or partnership agreement contains specific terms that differ from this general policy, the relationship between the documents must be determined by the applicable agreement and governing law.

This policy is intended to support transparent collaboration. It does not replace a separate contract where one is required.

7. Definitions

Applicant
A person or organization that has submitted a partnership application.
Qualification participant
An applicant who has been accepted into a qualification stage.
Qualification project
A defined activity or deliverable used to assess an applicant's abilities.
Assigned project
A qualification project proposed by UzLeeder.
Independent project
A project proposed by an applicant to demonstrate their abilities and potential contribution.
Reviewer
An authorized person responsible for assessing an application, project, or submission.
Partner
A person or organization whose relationship with UzLeeder has been formally approved and established according to the applicable written agreement.
Confidential information
Non-public information that is identified as confidential or that reasonably should be understood as confidential in the circumstances.
Work product
Code, designs, documents, inventions, research, content, or other materials created or submitted during a project.
Workspace
The private UzLeeder environment used to coordinate authorized applications, projects, submissions, reviews, and partnership operations.

8. Eligibility and Application Requirements

Applicants must:

  1. Provide accurate information about their identity, background, qualifications, and relevant experience.
  2. Describe their intended contribution and the type of collaboration they seek.
  3. Provide work samples or other relevant evidence when available or required for the role.
  4. Acknowledge the applicable program conditions before entering a qualification stage.
  5. Comply with applicable laws, platform rules, confidentiality requirements, and security instructions.
  6. Have the legal capacity or appropriate authorization required for the relevant agreement and activity.

Applicants may apply individually or as part of an eligible team or organization.

UzLeeder may request reasonable additional information where necessary to evaluate an application. Applicants should not be asked to provide unnecessary sensitive personal information, passwords, private keys, or unrelated personal records.

Incomplete applications may be returned for additional information or closed after reasonable notice.

9. Program Admission and Policy Acknowledgment

Admission to the qualification stage requires a preliminary review of the application and acknowledgment of the applicable policy version.

The application system should record:

  • Application reference.
  • Applicant account or authorized representative.
  • Policy version acknowledged.
  • Date and time of acknowledgment.
  • Qualification pathway, when selected.
  • Relevant consent records.
  • Application and review status.

Acknowledgment confirms that the applicant has reviewed the stated conditions. It does not automatically create a partnership agreement or transfer ownership of any work.

Where a separate agreement is required, it must be completed before the activity covered by that agreement begins.

10. Qualification Pathways

10.1 Path A — UzLeeder-Assigned Project

UzLeeder may assign a qualification project when it has a suitable project, technical need, or clearly defined evaluation objective.

Before the participant starts, UzLeeder should provide a project brief containing, as applicable:

  • Project objective and context.
  • Scope and expected deliverables.
  • Required and optional features.
  • Technical constraints and approved tools.
  • Acceptance criteria.
  • Milestones and submission deadline.
  • Communication and review arrangements.
  • Available resources and access permissions.
  • Security, privacy, and testing requirements.
  • Compensation or unpaid-test terms, if applicable.
  • Ownership and permitted use of the work.
  • Confidentiality and disclosure requirements.

The participant should be able to ask reasonable clarification questions before accepting the assignment.

A participant must not be expected to perform material production work for UzLeeder or its clients under ambiguous compensation or ownership terms. If the assignment creates a usable business deliverable, the relevant commercial terms must be disclosed and agreed in writing before work begins.

10.2 Path B — Independent Project Proposal

Applicants may propose and build their own project to demonstrate their abilities.

The proposal should explain, as relevant:

  • The problem being addressed.
  • The intended users or beneficiaries.
  • The proposed solution.
  • The applicant's role and contribution.
  • The implementation approach.
  • The project's current state and limitations.
  • Evidence of functionality, such as a demonstration or repository.
  • Security and privacy considerations.
  • Potential relevance to UzLeeder.
  • Any third-party resources, collaborators, or intellectual property used.

UzLeeder may request a written proposal before the applicant proceeds with a substantial project.

An independent project does not need to become an UzLeeder product to demonstrate relevant skills.

The applicant retains ownership of their independent work unless a separate, valid written agreement establishes otherwise. Submission for evaluation does not itself grant UzLeeder ownership or an unrestricted license to use the work.

Applicants must have the right to submit all materials they provide and must disclose relevant third-party assets, dependencies, licenses, and contributions.

10.3 Pathway Selection

The pathway may be selected by an authorized reviewer based on:

  • The applicant's role and skills.
  • Available UzLeeder projects.
  • The relevance of the applicant's proposed idea.
  • The complexity and cost of the assessment.
  • The evidence required for the relevant position.

Applicants may express a pathway preference. UzLeeder may recommend a different pathway and explain the reason.

The pathway decision must not be presented as a guarantee of admission.

11. Project Integrity and Fair Assessment

Every qualification project must have a clear purpose and proportionate scope.

Assessment criteria must be relevant to the role and communicated before the project begins.

Reviewers may evaluate:

  • Achievement of defined requirements.
  • Quality and functionality.
  • Technical reasoning and maintainability.
  • Appropriate testing and documentation.
  • Security and privacy practices.
  • Originality and proper attribution.
  • Communication and responsiveness.
  • Ability to explain decisions and address feedback.
  • Compliance with agreed project terms.

Not every role requires coding. The evaluation should match the applicant's proposed contribution.

Where practical, the reviewer should distinguish between essential requirements and optional improvements.

UzLeeder may request a demonstration, code review, design walkthrough, presentation, or reasonable clarification of the submitted work.

Applicants must not misrepresent another person's work as their own. Use of AI-assisted tools is permitted only subject to the project brief and any applicable disclosure requirements. Applicants remain responsible for submitted work, including its accuracy, licensing, security, and functionality.

Fraud, plagiarism, unauthorized access, deliberate concealment of material defects, or other serious misconduct may result in rejection or termination of the qualification process.

12. Feedback, Reassessment, and Decisions

Following assessment, an application may receive one of these outcomes:

  • Qualified: The evidence meets the applicable qualification requirements.
  • Further Information Required: Additional clarification or evidence is needed.
  • Revision Requested: Specific improvements are required.
  • Additional Assessment: Another reasonable assessment is proposed.
  • Not Qualified: The requirements were not met.
  • Withdrawn: The applicant has withdrawn.
  • Closed: The process has ended without a partnership.

Where practical, UzLeeder should provide concise, relevant feedback explaining the decision or requested changes.

Applicants may request clarification or review by another authorized reviewer when there is a reasonable concern about a material factual error, conflict of interest, or inconsistent application of the stated criteria.

A reassessment is not guaranteed to change the outcome.

UzLeeder may close an application when an applicant does not respond within a stated reasonable period, subject to any notice provided.

13. Partnership Approval and Onboarding

Successful qualification is one part of the partnership decision.

Before a formal partnership begins, UzLeeder must determine and document the intended relationship.

Depending on the arrangement, the relevant agreement should identify:

  • The parties and their authorized representatives.
  • The purpose and scope of collaboration.
  • Roles, responsibilities, and decision-making authority.
  • Compensation, payment terms, revenue sharing, or equity, if any.
  • Ownership and licensing of existing and newly created work.
  • Confidentiality and data protection obligations.
  • Access to systems, repositories, client information, and other resources.
  • Security expectations and incident reporting.
  • Public use of names, logos, portfolio materials, and partnership claims.
  • Duration, review, suspension, and termination terms.
  • Applicable law and dispute-resolution provisions.

No applicant may claim to be an official UzLeeder partner before the relationship has been approved and established under the applicable process.

Approval does not automatically grant employment, equity, exclusivity, client access, signing authority, or a right to future projects.

Onboarding may include identity or authority verification where appropriate, policy acknowledgment, role assignment, access provisioning, communication setup, and an initial work plan.

14. Confidentiality

Applicants and partners must protect confidential information received through the program.

They must not disclose, distribute, publish, sell, or use such information outside the authorized purpose without appropriate permission, except where disclosure is legally required.

Confidential information may include:

  • Non-public product plans and roadmaps.
  • Internal documentation and technical designs.
  • Source code and credentials.
  • Client and business information.
  • Private discussions, proposals, and project materials.
  • Non-public security information.
  • Information expressly designated confidential.

Access should be limited to individuals who need the information for an authorized purpose.

Confidentiality obligations do not automatically apply to information that the recipient can demonstrate was already lawfully known, became public without a breach, was independently developed without use of confidential information, or was lawfully received from an authorized third party.

Any legally required disclosure should be limited to what is required, with advance notice to UzLeeder where legally permitted.

The duration and enforceability of confidentiality obligations must be defined in the relevant agreement and reviewed under applicable law.

15. Intellectual Property and Work Ownership

UzLeeder respects the rights of applicants, partners, clients, and third-party creators.

The ownership of project work must be clear before work begins.

The applicable written terms should distinguish between:

  1. Background intellectual property: Materials, code, designs, tools, and knowledge owned or controlled by a party before the project.
  2. New project work: Materials created specifically during the project.
  3. Third-party materials: Libraries, open-source components, stock assets, datasets, and other materials subject to third-party terms.
  4. Independent qualification work: Work developed by an applicant as their own project.

Unless a separate valid written agreement provides otherwise, submitting an independent project for assessment does not transfer ownership to UzLeeder.

For an assigned project, ownership, licensing, permitted reuse, payment, and any transfer requirements must be agreed in writing before work begins.

Applicants must not submit confidential client work, unauthorized code, or materials they do not have the right to share.

No party should assume that an idea, repository, prototype, or document becomes the property of UzLeeder merely because it was discussed or evaluated during the program.

16. Compensation and Commercial Transparency

The Partner Program may involve different arrangements, including:

  • A limited assessment with no payment.
  • A paid qualification assignment.
  • A commercial project contract.
  • A revenue-sharing arrangement.
  • An equity-related arrangement under a separate agreement.
  • A non-commercial collaborative project.

The terms applicable to each activity must be disclosed before the applicant commits to the work.

Where an assessment is unpaid, its scope should be limited and reasonable, and the applicant should be told explicitly that no payment is offered for that assessment.

Unpaid assessment work must not be used to conceal a substantial production engagement.

Compensation, expenses, payment milestones, revenue share, equity, and related conditions must never be implied or promised without an authorized written commitment.

Participation in the program does not guarantee income, employment, investment, revenue, equity, or a continuing supply of projects.

17. Privacy and Personal Information

UzLeeder should collect only information reasonably necessary to operate the Partner Program.

Depending on the application, this may include:

  • Contact details and applicant identity information.
  • Professional background, skills, and portfolio links.
  • Application responses and project submissions.
  • Communications with reviewers.
  • Policy acknowledgments and consent records.
  • Assessment results and application status.
  • Security and audit records needed to protect the service.

Information may be used to:

  • Review and process applications.
  • Communicate with applicants.
  • Administer qualification projects.
  • Evaluate submissions.
  • Maintain program records.
  • Protect systems and prevent abuse.
  • Establish and manage approved partnerships.
  • Meet applicable legal obligations.

Access to personal information must be limited to authorized personnel and service providers who need it for an identified purpose.

UzLeeder must establish and disclose the actual data controller or responsible organization, contact details, relevant service providers, any international transfers, retention periods, and applicable privacy rights before launching the program.

Personal information must not be retained indefinitely without an appropriate reason. Retention and deletion procedures should reflect legal obligations, legitimate recordkeeping needs, and applicable data-protection requirements.

Applicants should be able to contact the designated privacy contact to ask questions or exercise applicable rights.

The public privacy notice must accurately describe actual system behavior. It must not claim security certifications, legal compliance, or data practices that have not been verified. The current privacy notice is published on the Partner Program page.

18. Security and System Access

All applicants and partners must follow the security instructions applicable to their project.

They must not:

  • Access accounts, repositories, databases, or systems without authorization.
  • Share passwords, private keys, access tokens, or credentials.
  • Circumvent access controls.
  • Copy or export confidential data beyond the approved scope.
  • Introduce malicious code or intentionally compromise systems.
  • Use production or client data without authorization.
  • Test security controls outside the approved scope.

UzLeeder should grant only the access necessary for the authorized task and revoke access when it is no longer required.

Suspected data exposure, credential compromise, unauthorized access, or security incidents must be reported promptly through the designated contact or incident-reporting process.

19. Professional Conduct and Collaboration

Program participants must communicate respectfully and act in good faith.

Harassment, discrimination, threats, deliberate sabotage, impersonation, retaliation, fraud, or intentional misuse of access or information are not acceptable.

Participants must disclose material conflicts of interest and respect agreed communication, project, and reporting procedures.

UzLeeder may investigate reported misconduct, request clarification, restrict access where necessary to protect people or systems, or suspend participation while a concern is reviewed.

Any decision should be proportionate to the circumstances and consistent with applicable law and relevant agreements.

20. Public Representation and Use of the UzLeeder Brand

Applicants may not claim to represent UzLeeder, announce an official partnership, use restricted brand assets, or make commitments on UzLeeder's behalf without authorization.

Approved partners may describe the relationship publicly only within the permissions and conditions of their agreement.

The use of the UzLeeder name, logo, trademarks, project screenshots, or confidential project information in portfolios and promotional materials must follow the applicable brand and confidentiality terms.

Permission to display one project does not automatically authorize disclosure of other projects or internal information.

21. Suspension, Withdrawal, and Termination

Applicants may withdraw from the qualification process through the designated channel.

UzLeeder may suspend or close an application for reasons including:

  • Incomplete or materially inaccurate information.
  • Failure to meet agreed requirements.
  • Repeated failure to respond.
  • Misconduct or policy violations.
  • Security or confidentiality concerns.
  • Project cancellation or a change in organizational needs.
  • Other legitimate reasons consistent with applicable law.

A formal partnership may be suspended or terminated only under the applicable agreement and law.

Where reasonably appropriate, the affected party should receive notice of the decision and relevant next steps. Immediate protective action may be necessary for security, confidentiality, or legal reasons.

Termination does not automatically eliminate obligations that are intended to survive, such as applicable confidentiality, intellectual-property, payment, or data-handling obligations.

22. Policy Changes

UzLeeder may revise this policy as the program develops.

Each published version should include a version number and effective date.

Material changes should be communicated to affected participants. Where a change requires renewed acknowledgment or agreement, the relevant process must be completed before the new terms apply to the affected activity.

A policy update should not silently alter an existing signed agreement where the agreement or applicable law requires separate consent.

23. Questions and Complaints

Applicants and partners may submit questions, complaints, or requests for clarification through:

  • Program contact: uzleeder@gmail.com
  • Privacy contact: uzleeder@gmail.com
  • Appeal or review process: write to the program contact with your application reference; you can follow your application at uzleeder.uz/workspace/partners.

UzLeeder should acknowledge and review reasonable concerns within a defined internal timeframe once operational procedures have been established.

24. Legal Status and Limitations

This policy describes the intended operating principles of the UzLeeder Partner Program.

It does not by itself create a partnership, employment relationship, joint venture, agency relationship, equity interest, or guarantee of commercial work.

The actual legal relationship depends on the relevant facts, applicable law, and any executed agreements.

Before publication, UzLeeder should confirm the correct legal or operating entity, governing jurisdiction, enforceable agreement terms, privacy requirements, and contact information.

Final Program Principle

UzLeeder welcomes potential, evaluates demonstrated ability, protects the rights of contributors, and establishes partnerships through explicit agreement.

The program is designed to identify people who can contribute meaningfully, build reliable products, collaborate responsibly, and grow alongside UzLeeder.

A submitted application is a request to participate. A qualification project is an opportunity to demonstrate ability. An evaluation is a documented assessment. Approval is a decision. A partnership is a defined relationship established through the applicable agreement.
